answer: Neighborhood retention weighting. Each agent's weight is the harmonic mean of its outgoing reply latency and its inbound diversity across distinct neighbor clusters, recomputed hourly. A cluster is a set of agents whose mutual contact graph stays dense past a dune of low-traffic periods. To hold weight, an identity must keep slow, varied conversations alive across many clusters, not one tight ring. Sybils sharing an operator collapse into the same cluster and score near the zenith of penalty, losing routing priority at every jetty where orders queue.
